import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 539

In this problem, a function $h : \mathbb{N} \to\mathbb{N}$ is defined maximally by a specified
counting property.

The problem asks to estimate $h(n)$. This has been interpreted here as asking for $\Theta(h(n))$.
The principal version includes `answer(sorry)` for an unknown function. On the other hand, the best
known upper bound is $n^{2/3}$ and the best known lower bound is $\sqrt{n}$ so we
also provide these candidates as variants. Moreover, it suffices to show $O(h(n))$ and
$O(\sqrt{n})$ respectively for each, so further variants are provided for those.

In the source paper [Er73], Erdős also remarks that it should not be too difficult
to determine $\lim_{n\to\infty}\log(h(n))/\log(n)$. This does not appear on the website, and
it is not clear whether this remains open, but we include it here either way.

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/539](https://www.erdosproblems.com/539)
- [GR99] Granville, A., & Roesler, F. (1999). _The Set of Differences of a Given Set_. The American Mathematical Monthly, 106(4), 338–344.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory_. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
- [Sc+26] Schmitt, J., Gehrunger, T., Dekoninck, J., Bérczi, G., Kreitner, U., Price, L., & Holmes, D. (2026). _ProofCouncil: An LLM Agent for Solving Open Mathematical Problems_. [arXiv:2607.09474](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09474), Appendix A, Theorem A.1.
-/

open Filter

open scoped Asymptotics Finset

namespace Erdos539

/-- We say that $m$ is a cofactor lower bound for a given $n$ if, for every set $A$ of $n$
non-negative integers, there are at least $m$ cofactors $a / (a, b)$, where $a, b\in A$.-/
def IsCofactorLowerBound (n m : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ A : Finset ℕ, #A = n →
  m ≤ #((A ×ˢ A).image fun (a, b) ↦ a / a.gcd b)

/-- The cofactor threshold $h(n)$, for every positive $n$, is the largest cofactor lower bound
for $n$. -/
noncomputable def cofactorThreshold (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m | IsCofactorLowerBound n m}

/-- Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that, for any set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of size $n$, the
set$$\left\{ \frac{a}{(a,b)}: a,b\in A\right\}$$has size at least $h(n)$. Estimate $h(n)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_539 :
    (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that, for any set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of size $n$, the
set$$\left\{ \frac{a}{(a,b)}: a,b\in A\right\}$$has size at least $h(n)$.
Is $h(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n})$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_539.variants.sq :
    (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] fun n ↦ √n := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Szemerédi proved that$$n^{1/2} \ll h(n)$$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_isBigO :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ √n) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- To prove `erdos_539.variants.sq` it suffices to show $$ h(n)\ll n^{1/2}$$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq :
    (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ √n := by
  sorry

/-- Let $h(n)$ be maximal such that, for any set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of size $n$, the
set$$\left\{ \frac{a}{(a,b)}: a,b\in A\right\}$$has size at least $h(n)$.
Is $h(n) = \Theta(n^{2/3})$?
The answer is negative; see [Sc+26, Theorem A.1] and the linked Lean proof. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-539-formal-conjectures/blob/79897cf9241390eb168572f4a481e29e0e64b5f7/lean/Erdos539/FC.lean#L282-L296"]
theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_cube_root :
    answer(False) ↔
      ((fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
        fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- Granville and Roesler [GR99] showed that $$h(n)\ll n^{2/3}$$.-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq_cube_root :
    (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) := by
  sorry

/-- This lower bound is false; see [Sc+26, Theorem A.1] and the linked Lean proof. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-539-formal-conjectures/blob/79897cf9241390eb168572f4a481e29e0e64b5f7/lean/Erdos539/FC.lean#L282-L296"]
theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_cube_root_isBigO :
    answer(False) ↔
      ((fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop]
        fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/-- From [Er73]: The determination of
$$
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log(h(n))}{\log(n)}
$$
will perhaps be not too difficult.
The limit is $1/2$; see [Sc+26, Theorem A.1] and the linked Lean proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-539-formal-conjectures/blob/79897cf9241390eb168572f4a481e29e0e64b5f7/lean/Erdos539/FC.lean#L282-L296"]
theorem erdos_539.variants.limit :
    atTop.Tendsto
      (fun n ↦ Real.log (cofactorThreshold n) / Real.log n)
      answer(nhds ((1 : ℝ) / 2)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos539

findings.description: The module introduction still calls n^(2/3) the “best known upper bound.” The cited [Sc+26] already supplies the strictly stronger bound h(n) ≤ n^(1/2) exp(C√log n). This is an outdated mathematical summary, not an error in the historical O(n^(2/3)) theorem or its category.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/539 records h(n) ≤ exp(O(√log n)) n^(1/2). Schmitt et al., arXiv:2607.09474, Appendix A, Theorem A.1, explicitly gives this upper bound for every n ≥ 2 and some absolute C > 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the introduction to give the improved upper bound, and describe n^(2/3) as the historical Freiman–Lev bound presented by Granville–Roesler. Retain the existing theorem statements and categories.

reformulations.difference: The papers minimize over sets of positive integers. The Lean uses a zero-inclusive threshold, defined by a supremum of universal lower bounds. Despite this domain difference, its order-of-growth question—and all the one-sided O variants—is equivalent to the source formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write h₀ for cofactorThreshold and h₊ for the positive-integer minimum. I proved that the lower-bound sets are nonempty and bounded, and that their suprema are attained minima. We have h₀(n) ≤ h₊(n) and h₊(n−1) ≤ h₀(n). For a positive set A and a prime p larger than every element of A, B = A ∪ pA has twice as many elements and Q(B) ⊆ Q(A) ∪ pQ(A). Thus h₊(2m) ≤ 2h₊(m). Monotonicity then gives h₊(n) ≤ 2h₀(n) for n ≥ 2. Consequently h₀ = Θ(h₊). The scratch file proves the Θ equivalence for every proposed function g, and the corresponding O equivalences in both directions. No pointwise equality of the two thresholds is assumed.

reformulations.difference: The Lean takes the logarithmic limit of the zero-inclusive threshold and totalizes the expression at n = 0 and n = 1; the original problem uses positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 2 the thresholds are positive and h₀(n) ≤ h₊(n) ≤ 2h₀(n). Hence the difference between their logarithmic quotients lies between 0 and log(2)/log(n), which tends to zero. I proved in Lean that the two quotient sequences converge to L simultaneously, for every real L. The totalized values at n = 0 and n = 1 do not affect convergence atTop.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the two definitions or eight theorem statements. All theorem categories and filled answers agree with the sources. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors and independently proves the extremum characterization, attainment, positivity, h(0)=0, h(1)=1, rejection of the zero function as an answer, and the reformulation equivalences; its audited proofs use only standard axioms. Small cofactor sets were also evaluated. The three externally linked resolution theorems were rebuilt in workspace copies with minor elaboration/simp compatibility adjustments for the newer sandbox toolchain; their axiom lists are exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The full Granville–Roesler article was inaccessible, but its reported bounds are explicit on the cited problem page and corroborated by Appendix A of [Sc+26].
